title: The API has no minimum-client-version gate and static runtime config/asset rollout policy is incomplete

original_titles.title: Runtime config.json, source-map tracker and asset caching policies unimplemented

problem: There is no X-Min-Client-Version enforcement or config.json/capability bootstrap contract. The server cannot require stale clients to refresh after a breaking API change, and cache/source-map rollout policy is not codified.
impact: A cached frontend can continue using a contract that the backend has already changed, causing hard-to-diagnose submission/auth failures.

verification.basis: Current source inspection at the main-branch commit listed in metadata. Original audit line numbers are treated as historical and were not reused as current line references.

implementation_steps.action: Publish a versioned runtime config/capability endpoint containing API minimum version and feature availability, with safe cache headers.
Send a frontend build version on API requests. Reject incompatible versions with 426 CLIENT_TOO_OLD before mutation.
Implement a reload/update UX that preserves locally saved drafts/outbox entries before reloading.
Define immutable asset caching with hashed filenames, short-lived HTML/config and a deliberate source-map upload/redaction strategy.
Test old-client behavior against a new minimum-version response.

acceptance_criteria: Old clients are detected before mutation and receive a safe update path.
Draft/outbox data survives a forced reload.
regression_tests: Add a focused failing test before implementation where practical.
Add a negative authorization / boundary test, not only a happy-path test.
Run the affected backend/frontend suite and the full CI workflow before merge.
